prediction.likelyOutcome: GSL should obtain summary judgment against Nguyen on the lease and guaranty — liability is essentially undisputed, the defendants filed no Civ.R. 56 response, and the identity argument fails under either construction. The realistic fight is over the size of the $104,295.80 itemization (mitigation/re-letting credit for the replacement tenant, and the open-term post-60-month CAM adjustment) and the unpleaded, unvalued conversion theory arising from the self-help lockout and $3,000 clean-out. Expect a judgment somewhat below the full $132,139.24 requested, with collectibility against a pro se guarantor as the larger practical risk.

outcome.description: On September 4, 2025 the trial court granted the landlord summary judgment for $132,139.24, exactly the sum itemized in the landlord's affidavit ($104,295.80 overdue rent and fees, $3,000 clean-out costs, $12,416.92 prejudgment interest, $12,010.52 attorneys' fees and $416 court costs), plus 8 percent post-judgment interest and collection fees; the amount recorded here is the judgment less the $12,010.52 in attorneys' fees. The Twelfth District affirmed on July 27, 2026, holding the guarantor forfeited his lockout, notarization and phantom-LLC arguments by not opposing the motion.
